# Development Environment

This project supports two ways of working. Pick whichever fits you. Both build
and test the same code; neither is required for the other.

The **recommended baseline is the minimal setup** — a text editor plus a few
open-source command-line tools. It is enough to build, run, and test the game.
The rich setup adds an IDE for people who want one.

> Setup recommendations here are not final. Only the requirement is fixed: a
> **minimal text-editor setup** and a **rich IDE setup** must both be documented.

## Shared prerequisites (both setups)

All target systems are Linux, macOS, and Windows, but the **primary platform is
Debian-based Linux** (Linux Mint, Ubuntu). Other systems are documented, not
tested regularly.

Common tools (all open source):

- **C++17 compiler** — GCC or Clang.
- **CMake** ≥ 3.15.
- **Git**.
- **SDL2 development files** — needed to build the game target.

### Debian / Ubuntu / Mint

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake git libsdl2-dev
```

### Fedora

```bash
sudo dnf install -y gcc-c++ make cmake git SDL2-devel
```

### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install cmake sdl2
```

### Windows

Use [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/) (open source) and, from a UCRT64 shell:

```bash
pacman -S --needed mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmake \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-SDL2 mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-ninja git
```

## Minimal setup (text editor)

You only need a text editor and a terminal. Good open-source editors:

- **Neovim** / **Vim** — with `clangd` for completion.
- **micro**, **Kate**, **Geany** — lightweight, no configuration.

### Build and test

```bash
git clone https://github.com/FreeOpenSourceSyndicate/FreeOpenSourceSyndicate.git
cd FOSSynd

# Full build (core + tests + game)
./scripts/build.sh

# Run the game
./build/src/FOSSynd

# Run the tests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

If you do not want the SDL2 dependency, build the core only:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=OFF
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

### Optional: language server

For completion and diagnostics without an IDE, install
[`clangd`](https://clangd.llvm.org/) and generate a compilation database:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
ln -s build/compile_commands.json compile_commands.json   # editors pick this up
```

## Rich setup (IDE)

Any of these work; all are open source.

### Visual Studio Code

1. Install VS Code and these extensions: **C/C++** (or **clangd**),
   **CMake Tools**.
2. Open the repository folder.
3. Let CMake Tools configure. If SDL2 is not found, set the CMake cache
   variable `FOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=OFF` to work on the core only.
4. Build with the CMake Tools toolbar; run tests from the **Testing** view.

### CLion

1. Open the repository folder; CLion detects `CMakeLists.txt`.
2. In **Settings → Build → CMake**, add `-DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON`.
3. Build and run the `FOSSynd` target; run `run_tests` for unit
   tests.

### Qt Creator

1. Open `CMakeLists.txt` as a project.
2. Add the CMake argument `-DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON`.
3. Build the `FOSSynd` target and run it.

### KDevelop

Open the folder, let it configure the CMake project, and build as usual.

## Running the game

```bash
./build/src/FOSSynd
```

Controls (prototype):

- **Left-click** a walkable tile — order the selected agent to move there.
- **Tab** — select the next agent.
- **Arrow keys** — scroll the view.
- **Esc** — quit.

Headless options (used by tests and CI):

```bash
./build/src/FOSSynd --headless --frames 30          # smoke test
./build/src/FOSSynd --headless --screenshot out.bmp # one frame to a BMP
```
